newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak blue chips mostly up, SAX firms 1.31 pts.
newsitem.headline: Slovak blue chips mostly up, SAX firms 1.31 pts.

text.p: Leading Slovak shares closed mostly higher in moderate trading on Bratislava Stock Exchange (BSE) on Thursday, helping the SAX index to firm 1.31 points to 201.60.
Brokers said activity seemed to be reviving, though they expected the SAX index to stay flat in the near future.
Steel producer VSZ Kosice gained 15 crowns to 645. Its average price during the session -- used for calculating the index -- rose by 2.09 percent, accounting most for the SAX's increase.

"The demand for VSZ share exceeds the supply on the market, and this drove its price a little higher at the close of today's trading to the more-real price levels," said Libor Briska of Creditanstalt.

Slovakia's largest commercial bank VUB closed up 50 crowns at 1,700, with its average price up 1.7 percent. Brokers said the small volume of traded shares made it hard for them to predict future trend in the price.
Oil and gas storage Nafta led trading activity with 15,700 shares traded, closing up two at 1,927 crowns, but traders said the large block traded was only a settlement of an earlier agreed deal.
Oil refiner Slovnaft was the only blue chip to post slight losses, closing down 10 crowns at 935.
"Slovnaft traded rather high volume of shares today, and the issue seems to be stable with the current price accepted both by buyers and sellers," Briska said.

Overall volume rose to 429,300 shares, from 384,057 shares traded on Wednesday, while the turnover fell to 239.19 million crowns, from 263.14 million on Wednesday. -- Peter Laca, Bratislava Newsroom, 42-7-563-3687
